definition.purpose: Practice generating several plausible explanations before settling on one.
definition.instruction: A parent has missed three scheduled visits with their child. Select every explanation that is plausible given only this information.
definition.accessibility_alternative: Options are a standard checkbox group.
definition.prompt: A parent has missed three scheduled visits with their child.

options.text: The visit location is hard to reach without a car.
options.why: Transportation is a common barrier and easy to check.

options.text: The parent's work schedule conflicts with the visit times.
options.why: Schedules set without the parent's input often clash with shift work.

options.text: The parent did not receive, or misunderstood, the notice.
options.why: Phone numbers change and instructions are easy to misread under stress.

options.text: The parent is avoiding visits out of fear, shame or distress.
options.why: Contact can be painful. Avoidance is possible, but it is still only a hypothesis.

options.text: The parent had a health problem or emergency.
The parent does not care about the child.
options.why: This is a conclusion about motive that the information does not support. Many other explanations fit the same facts.

definition.debrief: You usually cannot know which explanation is true yet. The skill is to keep several open and ask. Concluding indifference too early can lead to worse decisions and a weaker working relationship.
